title: A Trial to Compare the Pharmacokinetics of VNA-318 When Given as a Tablet or as a Liquid Suspension in Healthy Participants
official: A Phase 1, Open-label, Randomized, Single-dose Trial Investigating the Relative Bioavailability of a Tablet Formulation of VNA-318 Compared to the Powder for Suspension Formulation
summary:
The main goal of this Phase 1 study is to compare the pharmacokinetics of VNA-318 following a single 75 mg dose administered as a tablet and as a powder mixed into a liquid (oral suspension) in healthy male adults. Participants will receive both formulations in a randomly assigned sequence during Periods 1 and 2.

Following review of safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetic data from these periods, a Data Review Committee will determine whether Period 3 will be conducted and, if so, select an additional tablet dose.

Participants will undergo screening assessments, stay at the clinical center during each treatment period (for 3 overnight stays), return for follow-up visits, and complete an end-of-trial telephone contact.

Total participation may last up to 93 days, depending on the duration of the washout period before Period 3.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Trial participants are able and willing to provide written informed consent prior to any other clinical trial procedures.
2. Trial participants are able and willing to comply with all clinical trial requirements (including hospitalization periods, scheduled visits, trial intervention administration, clinical laboratory tests, other trial procedures, and lifestyle considerations) in accordance with the clinical trial protocol, ICH E6(R3) Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and applicable local regulations.
3. Healthy male.
4. Aged 18-55 years (inclusive) on the day of signing the Informed Consent Form (ICF).
5. Have a body mass index (BMI) between 18.5-30.0 kg / m2 (inclusive) at screening and P1D-1.
6. Have normal physical examination and vital signs results within normal ranges at screening and D˗1 of each period. If outside normal ranges, it must be considered by the Investigator without clinically significant abnormal findings.
7. Have a clinical laboratory of blood and urine within normal ranges at screening and D-1 of each period. If outside normal ranges, it must be considered by the Investigator without clinically significant abnormal findings.
8. Have 12-lead ECG results without clinically significant abnormal findings confirmed by the Investigator at screening and D-1 of each period.
9. Non-smoker (and no other nicotine use) as determined by history (no nicotine use over the past 6 months) and by urine cotinine concentration (\<200 ng / mL) at screening and D-1 of each period.
10. Have no problems with swallowing tablets.
11. If sexually active with a woman of childbearing potential and not sterile, the trial participant and his partner must commit to using a highly effective method of birth control starting at screening and throughout the entire trial and for 90 days after last dose of trial intervention administration:

    * Combined (estrogen and progestogen containing) hormonal contraception associated with inhibition of ovulation, started at least 4 weeks prior to the dosing (P1D1) and use of condom for the male partner.
    * Progestogen-only hormonal contraception associated with inhibition of ovulation, started at least 4 weeks prior to the dosing (P1D1) and use of condom for the male partner.
    * Intrauterine device placed at least 4 weeks prior to the dosing (P1D1), and use of condom for the male partner.
    * Intrauterine hormone-releasing system placed at least 4 weeks prior to the dosing (P1D1), and use of condom for the male partner.
    * Simultaneous use of a diaphragm or cervical cap with intravaginally applied spermicide and, for the male partner, a male condom.
    * Sexual abstinence (when in line with the preferred and usual trial participant's lifestyle).
    * Periodic abstinence (e.g., calendar, ovulation, symptothermal, post-ovulation methods) is not acceptable.
12. Trial participants must agree to abstain from sperm donation starting at screening and throughout the trial and for 90 days following their last dose of trial intervention administration.
13. Have competence in speaking, writing, and comprehending the local language where the trial is conducted.
14. Covered by a health insurance system where applicable, and / or in compliance with the recommendations of the national laws in force relating to research.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Any condition or disease detected during the medical interview / physical examination that could relapse during or immediately after the trial or would render the trial participant unsuitable for the trial, place the trial participant at undue risk, or interfere with the ability of the trial participant to complete the clinical trial, as determined by the Investigator.
2. Have a history of and / or current clinically significant disease / disorder determined by the Investigator: gastrointestinal, endocrine, renal, hepatic, immunological, cardiovascular, hematological, respiratory, neurologic, metabolic, urologic, dermatologic, psychiatric disorder, or allergic disease, hypersensitivity, or allergic reactions excluding mild asymptomatic seasonal allergies (either spontaneous or following drug administration), or malignancy (including lymphoma, leukemia, and skin cancer) unless remission over 10 years.
3. Have a personal or family history of prolonged QT interval syndrome or Torsade de Pointes, or family history of sudden death.
4. Have current presence of an illness, such as a common cold, isolated headache, diarrhea, etc., within 14 days prior to P1D1 that is categorized as clinically significant by the Investigator.
5. History or presence of regular use of recreational or illicit drugs within 1 year before trial P1D1.
6. Donation of blood or blood loss (i.e., \> 450 mL) within 90 days, or donated plasma within 7 days prior to P1D-1.
7. Known significant hypersensitivity or other contraindication to any of the components of the trial drug.
8. Have a positive test result for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), HCV antibody, or human immunodeficiency virus 1 and / or 2 antibodies (anti-HIV1 and anti-HIV2 Ab) at screening.
9. Positive findings of urine drug screen (methadone, barbiturates, amphetamines, methamphetamines, opiates (including morphine), cannabinoids, cocaine, benzodiazepines, tricyclic antidepressants (TCA), 3,4 methylenedioxymethamphetamine \[MDMA; ecstasy\]) at screening or D-1 of each period.
10. Have a positive alcohol breath test result at screening or D-1 of each period.
11. Have regular consumption of grapefruit juice and any xanthine-containing products (e.g., coffee, tea, chocolate, or Coca-Cola like drinks) more than six cups per day (or equivalent), or consumption of any xanthine-containing products alcoholic beverages within 48 h prior to dosing (D1) of each period and until final discharge day of each period, inclusive.
12. Have regular consumption of alcoholic beverages that exceed 21 units per week (1 unit = 10 g of pure alcohol).
13. Participation in any other interventional trial within ≤90 days prior to screening provided that the clinical trial did not entail administration of a biological compound with a long terminal phase half-life (t½), or in the exclusion period of a previous trial or participation in more than three clinical trials within the last 12 months.
14. Use of any prescribed or non-prescribed drugs (including vitamins, herbal and dietary supplements, e.g., St. John's Wort) within 2 weeks or 5 half-lives, whichever is longer, prior to trial drug administration, except for the occasional use of acetaminophen (up to 3 g / day), especially including those that lead to an increase of Nicotinamide Dinucleotide (NAD) levels.
15. Trial participants who, in the opinion of the Investigator, are not likely to complete the trial for whatever reason.
16. Trial participant is employed by Sponsor, the Contract Research Organization (CRO), or trial site (permanent, temporary contract worker, or designee responsible for the conduct of the trial) or is immediate family (i.e., a spouse, parent, sibling, or child, whether biological or legally adopted) of Sponsor, CRO, or trial site employee.
17. Prisoners or trial participants who are legally institutionalized and with rights restrictions.
